title: BiKA: Binarized KAN-inspired Neural Network for Efficient Hardware Accelerator Designs
problem: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks replace standard multiplication and activation functions with learnable nonlinear functions, which are complex to implement in hardware. Prior work lacks thorough exploration of lightweight KAN hardware accelerators suitable for edge devices.
motivation: KAN has potential to transform neural network design paradigm, and efficient hardware accelerators are critical for deploying neural networks on resource-constrained edge devices.
method: BiKA applies binarization to KAN architecture to reduce hardware complexity of learnable nonlinear functions. The approach uses binary weights and activations to simplify the nonlinear function computations while maintaining the KAN paradigm, enabling efficient hardware implementation for edge inference.
key_novelty: Combining binarization with KAN architecture to reduce hardware implementation complexity of learnable nonlinear functions while preserving KAN's potential benefits.
contributions: BiKA: a binarized KAN-inspired neural network architecture suitable for hardware acceleration
Hardware accelerator design methodology for efficient KAN-based inference on edge devices
Demonstration that binarization can reduce hardware resource consumption for KAN implementations
Exploration of emerging network structures (KAN) combined with quantization techniques for lightweight accelerators
limitations: Specific performance metrics, accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs, and detailed hardware resource consumption comparisons are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Efficient hardware acceleration for binarized KAN neural networks
